EPISTAXIS IN THE ED 
 
 
Immediate Management 
* ABCD approach  
* Ask the patient to blow their nose to remove all clots 
* Sit patient forward & ask them to pinch their nose  
  (press alae firmly against septum) for 10 – 15 minutes 
* Patient to spit out excess blood (swallowing will cause vomiting) 
* If bleeding stops à observe for 30 mins for re-bleeding 
* If no re-bleeding à Discharge  
* TTO: BactrobanÒ ointment apply 8 hourly for 3/7 
Still bleeding / Re-bleed 
Nasal Packing 
* Anaesthetise prior to packing  
 
Cotton wool soaked in 2% Lignocaine  
placed into the nose 
 
Nasal nerve block 
* MerocelÒ Nasal Tampon 
 
-Trim tampon if patient has a small nose 
 
-Insert along the floor of the nostril  
 
-Pack both nostrils à tamponade 
 
-Expand with adrenaline 1:10 000 
 
-Leave in situ for 24-48 hours 
* If no nasal tampons: 
-Soak a 10 x 10 cm piece of gauze in   
 CyclokapronÒ [500mg/5ml] – insert into   
 bleeding nostril 
 
-Pack with ribbon gauze soaked in bismuth 
Important information to note 
* Duration/frequency/side 
* Severity & estimated blood loss 
* Bleeding diathesis 
* Comorbidities 
* Current medication (oral/nasal) 
* History of recent trauma 
Still bleeding? 
Posterior bleed 
is likely 
Posterior Nasal Packing 
* Call a senior doctor 
* Administer CyclokapronÒ 15mg/kg (max 1g) IV over 15 min 
* Remove nasal packing 
* Insert a Foley’s catheter (size 10 – 14F) along the  
   floor of the nasal cavity until the tip is visualized in  
   the oropharynx. 
* Inflate Foley’s bulb with ±10-20ml of water for  
   injection. Retract catheter gently so that it butts  
   against the posterior palate.  
* Keep catheter in place by clamping with an umbilical  
   cord clamp. Place gauze around the umbilical cord clamp  
   as well as between the alar/nose & clamp to prevent   
   pressure necrosis. 
* Repack both nostrils with new anterior packing. 
* ENT Referral 
Admission Criteria 
* Elderly 
* Posterior nasal packing  
* COPD 
* Cardiac disorders 
Investigations 
* Blood tests are not routinely required 
* Excessive bleeding à Ward Hb 
* FBC/INR if: 
 
- Shocked 
- Age > 65 years 
- Pale 
 
- On Warfarin 
 
- Bleeding disorder 
Discharge Instructions 
* Counsel the patient on how to stop their   
   own bleeds (pinching nares for at least          
   15 minutes) 
* Avoid blowing nose, sniffing & nose  
   picking 
* Encourage nasal hydration 
       - Normal saline drops / Vaseline to keep  
         nostrils moist 
* If discharged with anterior packing in situ: 
       - refer within 48 hours for removal &  
         review at ENT OPD 
       - prophylactic antibiotics 
- AugmentinÒ oral for 3/7 
NO evidence between hypertension & epistaxis. 
Epistaxis is more common in hypertensive patients due to vascular fragility. 
Epistaxis & the associated anxiety cause an acute elevation in BP. 
Dr R Gihwala CMJAH Emergency Department June 2020
